A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Identifiable Latent Bandits work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original Synthetic and semi-synthetic ADCB experiments, including model-fitting results, sequential-decision performance, and appendix robustness analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds reward-noise experiments in Appendix E.4 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: Both retain contrastive LVM learning, OLS reward fitting, and CPG/FPG/FPG-TS decision rules. Explicit instance averaging in v5 matches v3 Appendix C. The FPG algebra and intercept revisions concern the derivation of the existing optimization, without establishing a changed implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a Synthetic test scenario with increasingly noisy reward feedback. The Synthetic and ADCB tasks remain, together with the earlier context-noise, latent-shift, non-Gaussian-noise, and nonlinear-reward scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 8a adds LinUCB to the ADCB comparison with latent noise N(0, 0.1); the corresponding v3 panel lacks it. Other existing comparator sets are retained. Although new Appendix E.4 mentions regression, Figure 9 displays only MAB, CPG, FPG, and FPG-TS.

E3.justification: The new reward-noise sweep fixes latent noise at N(0, 0.1) and uses levels labeled reward variance sigma = 0.5, 1, and 2. Existing splits, model settings, and training budgets remain. Equation 1 corrects the written cumulative-regret formula, without evidence that existing plotted results were recomputed.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.4 and Figure 9 test sensitivity to reward noise, distinguishing this from v3's existing context- and latent-noise analyses. The earlier distribution-shift, Age-removal, nonlinear-reward, arm-count, and non-Gaussian-noise analyses are retained, sometimes renumbered.

E5.justification: Both report one-standard-error bars using 200 or 1000 seeds and disclose 10-seed model-fitting runs. New Figure 9 follows the existing 200-seed reporting convention; no changed uncertainty-estimation practice or increase in existing run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds results showing greater reward-noise sensitivity for MAB and FPG approaching CPG's performance as noise increases. Figure 8a adds a poorly performing LinUCB curve. Tables 1, 3, and 4 and the matched pre-existing performance curves retain their values.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.5's constant-regret guarantee is narrowed from CPG and FPG to CPG, and Assumption 3.1(d) changes reward noise from sub-Gaussian to Gaussian. v5 removes the exponential-family corollary in v3 Appendix B.2, adds formal identifiability and affine-equivalence definitions, revises the affine-recovery proof, and corrects substantial FPG matrix/intercept algebra in Appendix D. Equation 1 also corrects the regret summation.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims: learning an identifiable continuous latent-bandit model from observational data, proposing three decision policies, and improving sample efficiency under identifying conditions. The detailed theoretical guarantee changes without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion now explicitly identifies stationarity and invertibility as key limitations and proposes time-dependent latent disease progression as future work. Section 3.3 clarifies CPG's independence from reward noise, while Appendix E.4 adds interpretation of FPG's relative robustness to noisy rewards.

D1.justification: v5 Appendix H newly discloses using L-BFGS for FPG and discusses forward-pass, running-average, optimization, and action-selection costs. The architectures, training hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime information otherwise match v3 Appendix I.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 revises its comparison with earlier latent-model assumptions. References add Basse and Bojinov (2020), Zhou and Brunskill (2016), and Abbasi-Yadkori et al. (2011), while removing Hyvarinen et al. (2019) and Tahami Monfared et al. (2023). The broader positioning among latent bandits, ICA, and causal inference remains.

P1.justification: v5 edits the abstract and selected explanatory paragraphs, reorganizes Section 3.3, rewrites Appendix F's introduction, and exchanges the order of Experimental Setup and LVM Results. These are localized narrative revisions; the main section sequence and most experimental discussion remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, extensively resizing and relocating figures, tables, and Algorithm 1. Figure 1 is revised and moved to the first page; Figure 9 adds three panels, and Figure 8a gains a legend entry. v5 also introduces running headers, including an uncorrected placeholder.

improvement.justification: v5 better aligns the constant-regret claim with the presented CPG proof and repairs portions of the affine-recovery and FPG derivations. The targeted reward-noise analysis and L-BFGS disclosure provide useful additional support. These gains are limited by remaining inconsistencies, including Appendix E.7's broad exponential-family assertion after removal of its corollary, incorrect cross-references, and placeholder headers.
